`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

228	### 4.2 MaskFormer.forward：两条路径的总调度
229	
230	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
231	
232	`forward` 是整个模型唯一的对外入口，长约 95 行，却浓缩了「一进两出」的结构：**公共前奏**（归一化、padding、backbone、head）之后按 `self.training` 二分——训练路径返回损失字典，推理路径返回逐图结果列表。理解它就拿到了整本手册的「总目录」：backbone 在 u3-l3、head 在 u3-l2、损失在单元五、三个推理分支在单元六逐一展开。
233	
234	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
235	
236	```text
237	forward(batched_inputs)
238	│
239	├─ 公共前奏
240	│   1. 每张图 .to(device)
241	│   2. (x - pixel_mean) / pixel_std          # 逐通道归一化
242	│   3. ImageList.from_tensors(images, size_divisibility=32)
243	│      → 把 batch 内所有图 pad 到同一 H_pad×W_pad（32 的倍数）
244	│      → image_sizes 记录各自 pad 前的 (H, W)
245	│   4. features = backbone(images.tensor)    # {"res2":…, "res3":…, "res4":…, "res5":…}
246	│   5. outputs = sem_seg_head(features)      # {"pred_logits":(B,Q,134),
247	│                                             #  "pred_masks":(B,Q,H/4,W/4),
248	│                                             #  "aux_outputs":[…9 个…]}
249	│
250	├─ if self.training:                    ──── 训练路径
251	│   6. 取出每图 "instances" → prepare_targets → targets
252	│   7. losses = criterion(outputs, targets)   # 30 个键
253	│   8. 按 criterion.weight_dict 加权；不在 weight_dict 里的键直接删除
254	│   9. return losses                          # dict[str, Tensor]
255	│
256	└─ else:                                ──── 推理路径
257	   10. mask_pred 上采样：1/4 分辨率 → padding 尺寸（双线性）
258	   11. del outputs 释放中间结果
259	   12. 逐图循环：
260	       ├─ sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference?
261	       │    是 → 先把 mask 还原到原图 (height, width)
262	       ├─ SEMANTIC_ON  → semantic_inference  → result["sem_seg"]
263	       ├─ PANOPTIC_ON  → panoptic_inference  → result["panoptic_seg"]
264	       └─ INSTANCE_ON  → instance_inference  → result["instances"]
265	   13. return processed_results               # list[dict]
266	```
267	
268	三种尺寸必须分清（u6-l1 也强调过）：
269	
270	| 名称 | 来源 | 典型值（demo，最短边 800） |
271	|---|---|---|
272	| 原图尺寸 | `batched_inputs[i]["height"/"width"]` | 例如 1332×800 |
273	| 网络输入尺寸 | mapper/预测器缩放后、padding 前 | 例如 800×1200 |
274	| padding 尺寸 | `images.tensor.shape[-2:]`（32 的倍数） | 例如 800×1216 |

282	```python
283	images = [x["image"].to(self.device) for x in batched_inputs]
284	images = [(x - self.pixel_mean) / self.pixel_std for x in images]
285	images = ImageList.from_tensors(images, self.size_divisibility)

288	归一化常数来自 `_BASE_` 配置的 `PIXEL_MEAN [123.675, 116.280, 103.530]`、`PIXEL_STD [58.395, 57.120, 57.375]`（[Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml:6-7](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml#L6-L7)），RGB 顺序。`ImageList.from_tensors` 是 detectron2 提供的工具：把 batch 内尺寸不一的图全部 pad 到「最大高、最大宽、且被 `size_divisibility` 整除」的统一画布上，右侧/下侧补零，并把各自 pad 前的 `(H, W)` 存进 `images.image_sizes`。注意 LSJ 训练时输入恒为 1024×1024（u2-l3），本来就是 32 的倍数，padding 实际是零开销；推理时图片尺寸任意，padding 才真正发挥作用。

414	### 4.3 prepare_targets：把 Instances 变成 labels + masks
415	
416	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
417	
418	criterion 的输入不是 detectron2 的 `Instances`，而是朴素的 `list[dict]`，每图一个 dict，只含两个键：`"labels"`（该图 N 个 GT 的连续类别 id，形状 `(N,)`）和 `"masks"`（二值 mask 张量，形状 `(N, H_pad, W_pad)`）。`prepare_targets` 就是这最后一跳的「格式转换器」。
419	
420	最关键的设计决策：GT mask 的尺寸适配用的是 **左上角对齐 zero-pad**，而不是 resize。原因：u2-l3 讲过 mapper 输出的 `gt_masks` 已经是网络输入尺寸（LSJ 下 1024×1024）的 tensor，与图像经受的几何变换完全一致；到 padding 尺寸只差右侧/下侧补零，与 `ImageList` 对图像的处理方式完全对称——**图像怎么 pad，GT 就怎么 pad**。如果用插值 resize，GT mask 的二值边界会被破坏，且与图像网格错位。
421	
422	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
423	
424	```text
425	prepare_targets(targets=list[Instances], images=ImageList)
426	  h_pad, w_pad = images.tensor.shape[-2:]        # padding 尺寸
427	  for 每张图的 Instances:
428	      gt_masks = instances.gt_masks               # (N, H, W) tensor
429	      padded = zeros(N, h_pad, w_pad)             # 全 0 画布
430	      padded[:, :H, :W] = gt_masks                # 左上角原样贴入
431	      new_targets.append({
432	          "labels": instances.gt_classes,         # (N,)
433	          "masks":  padded,                       # (N, H_pad, W_pad)
434	      })
435	  return new_targets
436	```
437	
438	注意 batch 内每张图的 N 可以不同（图片里对象数不同），`labels`/`masks` 是按图成对的列表，匹配与损失都按图处理后汇总（criterion 里 `num_masks = sum(len(t["labels"]) for t in targets)`，见 [criterion.py:225](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/criterion.py#L225)）。
439	
440	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
441	
442	[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:264-278](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L264-L278)
443	
444	```python
445	def prepare_targets(self, targets, images):
446	    h_pad, w_pad = images.tensor.shape[-2:]          # ① padding 尺寸
447	    new_targets = []
448	    for targets_per_image in targets:
449	        # pad gt
450	        gt_masks = targets_per_image.gt_masks        # ② (N, H, W) tensor（来自 mapper）
451	        padded_masks = torch.zeros(
452	            (gt_masks.shape[0], h_pad, w_pad),
453	            dtype=gt_masks.dtype, device=gt_masks.device)   # ③ 新画布，类型/设备对齐
454	        padded_masks[:, : gt_masks.shape[1], : gt_masks.shape[2]] = gt_masks  # ④ 左上角贴入
455	        new_targets.append(
456	            {
457	                "labels": targets_per_image.gt_classes,     # ⑤ 连续类别 id
458	                "masks": padded_masks,
459	            }
460	        )
461	    return new_targets
462	```
463	
464	- ① 尺寸取自 `images.tensor` 而不是原图——GT mask 必须与 `pred_masks` 上采样后共享同一画布，损失才能逐像素对齐。
465	- ② `gt_masks` 是**tensor**。LSJ mapper 里 `instances.gt_masks = masks.tensor`（`BitMasks` 的裸 tensor，见 [coco_panoptic_new_baseline_dataset_mapper.py:157-160](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/data/dataset_mappers/coco_panoptic_new_baseline_dataset_mapper.py#L157-L160)）；如果喂进来的是 `PolygonMasks`（多边形列表，无 `.shape[1]`/`.shape[2]`），第 ④ 行会直接 `AttributeError`/索引错误——这是自己写 mapper 时最常见的坑。
466	- ③ `torch.zeros` 保证 pad 区是 0（非对象），`dtype`/`device` 与 GT 一致。
467	- ④ 切片赋值：`[:, :H, :W]` 把整张 GT mask 不做任何缩放地放到画布左上角，右侧/下侧留 0。
468	- ⑤ `gt_classes` 是 mapper 阶段已映射好的**连续 id**（0..132），与 `pred_logits` 的前 K 维直接对应；全景标注原始的 `category_id` 到连续 id 的映射发生在数据注册/mapper 侧（u2-l2、u2-l3），到这里已经是干净的张量。
469	
470	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
471	
472	**实践目标**：构造玩具 `Instances`，调用 `prepare_targets`，亲眼验证 pad 行为与输出结构。
473	
474	**操作步骤**（示例代码，需要已安装 detectron2；不需要编译 MSDeformAttn 算子，因为我们不构建完整模型，只借 `Instances` 和 `ImageList`）：

476	```python
477	# 示例代码：独立验证 prepare_targets
478	import torch
479	from detectron2.structures import Instances, ImageList
480	
481	# 1) 仿照模型属性拼两个最小依赖
482	h_pad, w_pad = 64, 96   # 假装 padding 尺寸是 64x96（size_divisibility=32 的倍数）
483	
484	class FakeModel:
485	    def prepare_targets(self, targets, images):  # 复制 maskformer_model.py L264-L278 的实现
486	        h_pad, w_pad = images.tensor.shape[-2:]
487	        new_targets = []
488	        for t in targets:
489	            gt_masks = t.gt_masks
490	            padded = torch.zeros((gt_masks.shape[0], h_pad, w_pad),
491	                                 dtype=gt_masks.dtype, device=gt_masks.device)
492	            padded[:, : gt_masks.shape[1], : gt_masks.shape[2]] = gt_masks

494	        return new_targets
495	
496	# 2) 造一张 50x70 的"图"，2 个 GT 对象
497	inst = Instances((50, 70))
498	inst.gt_classes = torch.tensor([3, 128])
499	inst.gt_masks = torch.zeros(2, 50, 70)
500	inst.gt_masks[0, :20, :30] = 1.0   # 对象 0：左上角一块
501	inst.gt_masks[1, 40:, 60:] = 1.0   # 对象 1：右下角一块
502	
503	images = ImageList(torch.zeros(1, 3, h_pad, w_pad), image_sizes=[(50, 70)])

505

508	print(int(out["masks"][0].sum()))                  # 期望 600 = 20*30

518	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
519	
520	**练习 1**：如果某图的 GT mask 尺寸大于 padding 尺寸（例如手工喂数据时忘了先做 LSJ resize），会发生什么？
521	
522	**答案**：第 ④ 行切片赋值中 `gt_masks.shape[1] > h_pad` 时，`padded_masks[:, :H, :W]` 的目标区域比源小，PyTorch 会因形状不匹配抛 `RuntimeError`。这天然起到了「GT 必须与图像同尺寸」的断言作用。
523	
524	**练习 2**：为什么 pad 出来的全 0 背景对损失是「正确的」监督信号，而不是「噪声」？
525	
526	**答案**：`ImageList` 对图像 pad 的区域同样是 0，模型在这些像素上的预测没有任何图像依据；GT mask 在此处为 0 表示「不属于任何对象」，恰好与「预测的所有 mask 在此处都应接近 0」对应。更重要的是，匈牙利匹配在 mask 代价里会避开纯背景差异的歧义（u5-l1 详解）。反过来说，batch 内不同图的 padding 量不同，若用全图逐像素损失而不加处理，短图会被更多 pad 区稀释——这就是 criterion 里按「mask 数量」而非「像素数」归一化的动机之一（u5-l2 详解）。
527	
528	**练习 3**：`prepare_targets` 为什么需要 `images` 参数？只用 `batched_inputs` 里的信息不够吗？
529	
530	**答案**：`batched_inputs[i]["image"]` 的形状是 padding **前**的网络输入尺寸，而 GT mask 必须落在 padding **后**的画布上（与 `images.tensor`、上采样后的 `pred_masks` 对齐）。`H_pad/W_pad` 只有 `ImageList` 知道，所以必须把 `images` 传进来。

# u3-l1｜MaskFormer 顶层 Meta Architecture

> 依赖讲义：u1-l5（配置系统）、u2-l1（train_net.py 主流程）。本讲正式进入模型内部，从最顶层的 `MaskFormer` 类开始。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 画出 `MaskFormer.forward` 的完整流程图：图像归一化 → ImageList padding → backbone → sem_seg_head → 训练/推理两条分支。
2. 说出 `from_config` 里构建了哪几个组件、`weight_dict` 是怎么从 3 个损失键膨胀成 30 个键的。
3. 逐行解释 `prepare_targets` 如何把 detectron2 的 `Instances` 变成 `{"labels": ..., "masks": ...}` 字典，并解释为什么 GT mask 是「左上角对齐 zero-pad」而不是 resize。
4. 独立完成一个实践：不加载权重构建 COCO 全景分割配置的 `MaskFormer`，分别在 train/eval 模式下对随机输入跑前向，打印两种模式返回的键。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 meta architecture：detectron2 对「一个完整模型」的抽象

detectron2 把「一个可以直接 `model(inputs)` 调用的完整模型」叫做 **meta architecture**。u1-l3 讲过「import 即注册」：`import mask2former` 时，装饰器 `@META_ARCH_REGISTRY.register()` 把 `MaskFormer` 类登记进 detectron2 的注册表；之后无论是 `train_net.py` 的 Trainer 还是 demo 里的 `DefaultPredictor`，都通过 `build_model(cfg)` 按 `cfg.MODEL.META_ARCHITECTURE`（这里取值 `"MaskFormer"`）从注册表取类并实例化。

### 2.2 mask classification 范式一分钟回顾

传统分割对每个像素问「你是哪一类」（per-pixel classification）；Mask2Former 换成对每个像素问「你属于哪个对象」，即 **mask classification**：模型输出 \(Q\) 个 query（COCO 配置里 \(Q=100\)），每个 query 负责预测

- 一个类别分布 `pred_logits`，形状 `(B, Q, K+1)`，最后一维多出的 1 是 **no-object 通道**（这个 query 没对上任何真实对象的出口）；
- 一个 mask `pred_masks`，形状 `(B, Q, H/4, W/4)`（mask 特征图是 1/4 分辨率）。

本讲的 `MaskFormer` 类不关心这些预测怎么算出来（那是 sem_seg_head 的事，u3-l2 起细讲），它只负责「调度」：喂数据、分损失或分推理。

### 2.3 forward 的输入契约：batched_inputs

`forward(batched_inputs)` 接收的是 **list[dict]**，每个 dict 对应一张图。这是 detectron2 全链路的通用格式——u2-l3 讲过 DatasetMapper 的输出就是它：

| 键 | 出现场合 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| `"image"` | 总是存在 | `(C, H, W)` 张量，已缩放到网络输入尺寸、已转 RGB |
| `"height"` / `"width"` | 总是存在 | **原图**的高宽（mapper 透传），推理后处理时用 |
| `"instances"` | 训练时 | `Instances` 对象，含 `gt_classes`、`gt_masks`（tensor，`(N, H, W)`） |

同一份契约同时服务训练（dataloader）和推理（`DefaultPredictor`），这是 `forward` 内部用 `self.training` 分流的根本前提。

### 2.4 train()/eval() 与 self.training

`nn.Module` 自带布尔标志 `self.training`：`model.train()` 置 True，`model.eval()` 置 False（还会联动把 BN/Dropout 切到推理行为）。detectron2 的引擎在训练循环里保证模型处于 train 模式、评估时切 eval 模式，所以 `MaskFormer.forward` 里只需要读 `self.training` 一个布尔值就能分流。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
|---|---|---|
| [mask2former/maskformer_model.py](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py) | `MaskFormer` 顶层模型，本讲主角 | `from_config`、`forward`、`prepare_targets` |
| [mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py) | sem_seg_head：组装像素解码器与 Transformer 解码器 | 只看 `layers` 的输出契约（u3-l2 再拆） |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲拆三个最小模块：**4.1 from_config**（模型怎么被造出来）、**4.2 MaskFormer.forward**（模型怎么跑）、**4.3 prepare_targets**（训练分支里最关键的一步格式转换）。

---

### 4.1 from_config：从一份 cfg 到一个可训练的模型

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

u1-l5 讲过配置五层叠加，u2-l1 讲过 `build_model` 交给注册表。中间还有一环：detectron2 的 `@configurable` 装饰器约定，`build_model(cfg)` 实际执行的是 `cls.from_config(cfg)`，它返回一个 **参数字典**，再用这个字典调用 `__init__`。

这样设计的好处：`__init__` 保留纯 PyTorch 风格（显式参数、可类型标注、可脱离 detectron2 单测），而「读哪些配置键、怎么组装子模块」全部集中在 `from_config`。你以后自定义组件时也要遵守这个模式。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
build_model(cfg)
  └─ META_ARCH_REGISTRY["MaskFormer"].from_config(cfg)
       1. build_backbone(cfg)                      → R50（或 Swin）
       2. build_sem_seg_head(cfg, backbone.output_shape())
                                                   → MaskFormerHead（u3-l2）
       3. HungarianMatcher(cost_class=2.0, cost_mask=5.0, cost_dice=5.0,
                           num_points=12544)        → 匹配器
       4. weight_dict = {loss_ce:2.0, loss_mask:5.0, loss_dice:5.0}
          + DEEP_SUPERVISION 时按层展开 _0.._8 后缀  → 3 + 9×3 = 30 个键
       5. SetCriterion(num_classes=133, matcher, weight_dict,
                       eos_coef=0.1, losses=["labels","masks"], ...)
       6. return {...全部参数...} → __init__(**kwargs)
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 构建两大可学习组件：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:98-99](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L98-L99)

```python
backbone = build_backbone(cfg)
sem_seg_head = build_sem_seg_head(cfg, backbone.output_shape())
```

先建 backbone，再把 `backbone.output_shape()`（各层通道数/步长信息）喂给 sem_seg_head 的构建函数——head 据此知道输入特征长什么样，通道自动对齐，这是「换 backbone 不改 head 代码」的关键（u8-l1 扩展实践的基础）。

**② 构造匹配器与损失权重：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:106-125](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L106-L125)

```python
class_weight = cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.CLASS_WEIGHT   # 2.0
dice_weight  = cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.DICE_WEIGHT    # 5.0
mask_weight  = cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.MASK_WEIGHT    # 5.0

matcher = HungarianMatcher(
    cost_class=class_weight, cost_mask=mask_weight, cost_dice=dice_weight,
    num_points=cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TRAIN_NUM_POINTS,   # 12544
)

weight_dict = {"loss_ce": class_weight, "loss_mask": mask_weight, "loss_dice": dice_weight}

if deep_supervision:
    dec_layers = cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.DEC_LAYERS        # 10
    aux_weight_dict = {}
    for i in range(dec_layers - 1):                      # i = 0..8
        aux_weight_dict.update({k + f"_{i}": v for k, v in weight_dict.items()})
    weight_dict.update(aux_weight_dict)
```

注意三个权重**同时**扮演两个角色：构造匹配器的代价系数、构造损失的加权系数——论文里匹配代价与损失权重共享数值，源码里就是这同一个变量传两处。

深监督展开：`DEC_LAYERS: 10` 的注释写着 "9 decoder layers, add one for the loss on learnable query"（见 [maskformer2_R50_bs16_50ep.yaml:36](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/maskformer2_R50_bs16_50ep.yaml#L36)），所以辅助键是 `_0` 到 `_8` 共 9 组。最终

\[ |\text{weight\_dict}| = 3 \times (1 + (\text{DEC\_LAYERS}-1)) = 3 \times 10 = 30 \]

这正是 u2-l1 里「训练日志有 30 个 loss 键」的出处。

**③ 组装 SetCriterion：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:129-138](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L129-L138)

`num_classes` 直接取 `sem_seg_head.num_classes`（COCO 全景为 133 = 80 thing + 53 stuff），保证头和损失永远用同一个类别数；`eos_coef=NO_OBJECT_WEIGHT=0.1` 给 no-object 类降权；`losses=["labels", "masks"]` 声明只用这两种损失。

**④ 返回参数字典（含推理开关的联动逻辑）：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:140-161](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L140-L161)

```python
return {
    "backbone": backbone,
    "sem_seg_head": sem_seg_head,
    "criterion": criterion,
    "num_queries": cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.NUM_OBJECT_QUERIES,     # 100
    "object_mask_threshold": cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.OBJECT_MASK_THRESHOLD,
    "overlap_threshold": cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.OVERLAP_THRESHOLD,
    "metadata": MetadataCatalog.get(cfg.DATASETS.TRAIN[0]),
    "size_divisibility": cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.SIZE_DIVISIBILITY,
    "sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference": (
        cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.SEM_SEG_POSTPROCESSING_BEFORE_INFERENCE
        or cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.PANOPTIC_ON
        or cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.INSTANCE_ON
    ),
    ...
    "semantic_on":  cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.SEMANTIC_ON,
    "instance_on":  cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.INSTANCE_ON,
    "panoptic_on":  cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TEST.PANOPTIC_ON,
    "test_topk_per_image": cfg.TEST.DETECTIONS_PER_IMAGE,
}
```

两处值得注意：

- `metadata` 取**训练集**的元数据（类别名、thing/stuff 划分），推理时全景/实例分支靠它判断「这个类是不是 thing」。COCO 配置里训练集是 `coco_2017_train_panoptic`（见 [Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml:16-18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml#L16-L18)）。
- `sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference` 是「显式配置 or 全景开 or 实例开」：只要做全景/实例推理，就必须先把 mask 还原到原图尺寸再推理（这两个分支要逐像素硬分配），这个三值 or 就是强制开关的落点。

**⑤ `__init__` 只做记账，不建任何可学习子模块：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:71-94](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L71-L94)

把传进来的组件挂到 `self.`，注册 `pixel_mean/pixel_std` 为 buffer（`persistent=False`，不进 checkpoint），处理 `size_divisibility < 0` 时回退到 backbone 自带的值，最后一条断言：

```python
if not self.semantic_on:
    assert self.sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference
```

语义关（只做全景/实例）时**必须**先还原尺寸——呼应上面第 ④ 点的 or 逻辑。

另外 [mask2former_model.py:163-165](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L163-L165) 的 `device` property 从 `pixel_mean` 所在设备取设备号，forward 里 `x["image"].to(self.device)` 就靠它。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`from_config` 里 `num_classes` 为什么取 `sem_seg_head.num_classes` 而不是再读一次 `cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.NUM_CLASSES`？

**答案**：单一事实来源。`MaskFormerHead.__init__` 已把该配置存为 `self.num_classes`（[mask_former_head.py:85](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py#L85)），从 head 取值保证头与损失永远一致；若两处各读一次配置，将来一处改了另一处漏改就会出现类别数不匹配。

**练习 2**：如果某配置 `TEST.PANOPTIC_ON: False`、`TEST.INSTANCE_ON: False`、`TEST.SEM_SEG_POSTPROCESSING_BEFORE_INFERENCE` 未设置（默认 False），`sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference` 最终是 True 还是 False？这带来什么行为？

**答案**：False（三个条件全 False）。此时语义推理走「低分辨率融合、后置还原尺寸」路径，避免先物化 Q 张高清 mask 导致的显存暴涨——这正是 u6-l1 讲过的 OOM 规避取舍。

**练习 3**：`HungarianMatcher` 的 `num_points=12544` 从哪个配置键来？它在匹配器里干什么？

**答案**：来自 `cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TRAIN_NUM_POINTS`。匹配器在计算 mask 代价时不逐像素比 mask，而是在随机+重要性采样的 12544 个点上近似（u5-l1 精讲），这是 memory-efficient 的关键设计。

### 4.2 MaskFormer.forward：两条路径的总调度

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`forward` 是整个模型唯一的对外入口，长约 95 行，却浓缩了「一进两出」的结构：**公共前奏**（归一化、padding、backbone、head）之后按 `self.training` 二分——训练路径返回损失字典，推理路径返回逐图结果列表。理解它就拿到了整本手册的「总目录」：backbone 在 u3-l3、head 在 u3-l2、损失在单元五、三个推理分支在单元六逐一展开。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
forward(batched_inputs)
│
├─ 公共前奏
│   1. 每张图 .to(device)
│   2. (x - pixel_mean) / pixel_std          # 逐通道归一化
│   3. ImageList.from_tensors(images, size_divisibility=32)
│      → 把 batch 内所有图 pad 到同一 H_pad×W_pad（32 的倍数）
│      → image_sizes 记录各自 pad 前的 (H, W)
│   4. features = backbone(images.tensor)    # {"res2":…, "res3":…, "res4":…, "res5":…}
│   5. outputs = sem_seg_head(features)      # {"pred_logits":(B,Q,134),
│                                             #  "pred_masks":(B,Q,H/4,W/4),
│                                             #  "aux_outputs":[…9 个…]}
│
├─ if self.training:                    ──── 训练路径
│   6. 取出每图 "instances" → prepare_targets → targets
│   7. losses = criterion(outputs, targets)   # 30 个键
│   8. 按 criterion.weight_dict 加权；不在 weight_dict 里的键直接删除
│   9. return losses                          # dict[str, Tensor]
│
└─ else:                                ──── 推理路径
   10. mask_pred 上采样：1/4 分辨率 → padding 尺寸（双线性）
   11. del outputs 释放中间结果
   12. 逐图循环：
       ├─ sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference?
       │    是 → 先把 mask 还原到原图 (height, width)
       ├─ SEMANTIC_ON  → semantic_inference  → result["sem_seg"]
       ├─ PANOPTIC_ON  → panoptic_inference  → result["panoptic_seg"]
       └─ INSTANCE_ON  → instance_inference  → result["instances"]
   13. return processed_results               # list[dict]
```

三种尺寸必须分清（u6-l1 也强调过）：

| 名称 | 来源 | 典型值（demo，最短边 800） |
|---|---|---|
| 原图尺寸 | `batched_inputs[i]["height"/"width"]` | 例如 1332×800 |
| 网络输入尺寸 | mapper/预测器缩放后、padding 前 | 例如 800×1200 |
| padding 尺寸 | `images.tensor.shape[-2:]`（32 的倍数） | 例如 800×1216 |

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 归一化与 ImageList：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:193-195](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L193-L195)

```python
images = [x["image"].to(self.device) for x in batched_inputs]
images = [(x - self.pixel_mean) / self.pixel_std for x in images]
images = ImageList.from_tensors(images, self.size_divisibility)
```

归一化常数来自 `_BASE_` 配置的 `PIXEL_MEAN [123.675, 116.280, 103.530]`、`PIXEL_STD [58.395, 57.120, 57.375]`（[Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml:6-7](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/Base-COCO-PanopticSegmentation.yaml#L6-L7)），RGB 顺序。`ImageList.from_tensors` 是 detectron2 提供的工具：把 batch 内尺寸不一的图全部 pad 到「最大高、最大宽、且被 `size_divisibility` 整除」的统一画布上，右侧/下侧补零，并把各自 pad 前的 `(H, W)` 存进 `images.image_sizes`。注意 LSJ 训练时输入恒为 1024×1024（u2-l3），本来就是 32 的倍数，padding 实际是零开销；推理时图片尺寸任意，padding 才真正发挥作用。

**② 前向计算：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:197-198](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L197-L198)

```python
features = self.backbone(images.tensor)     # dict: res2..res5
outputs = self.sem_seg_head(features)       # dict: pred_logits / pred_masks / aux_outputs
```

两行就是「三大组件」的前两个。`MaskFormerHead.layers` 的返回值直接透传 Transformer 解码器的输出字典（契约见 [mask_former_head.py:118-132](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/meta_arch/mask_former_head.py#L118-L132)），所以 `outputs` 的键由解码器决定：`pred_logits`、`pred_masks`、`aux_outputs`。

**③ 训练分支：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:200-217](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L200-L217)

```python
if self.training:
    if "instances" in batched_inputs[0]:
        gt_instances = [x["instances"].to(self.device) for x in batched_inputs]
        targets = self.prepare_targets(gt_instances, images)
    else:
        targets = None

    losses = self.criterion(outputs, targets)

    for k in list(losses.keys()):
        if k in self.criterion.weight_dict:
            losses[k] *= self.criterion.weight_dict[k]
        else:
            losses.pop(k)
    return losses
```

要点：

- `criterion(outputs, targets)` 内部先做匈牙利匹配，再逐损失计算，最后对 `aux_outputs` 里 9 个中间层逐层重匹配重计算，返回的字典键正是 4.1 里那 30 个（见 [criterion.py:212-247](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/criterion.py#L212-L247)）。
- 末尾的循环是**加权 + 过滤**一体：在 `weight_dict` 里的键乘上权重；不在的（例如未来给 criterion 加的新损失忘了配权重）直接从字典删除——防止未加权损失混进日志误导调参。
- detectron2 的引擎把返回 dict 的各项求和当作总 loss 反传，日志逐键打印。

**④ 推理分支：上采样 + 三开关分发：**

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:218-234](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L218-L234)

```python
mask_cls_results = outputs["pred_logits"]     # (B, Q, K+1)
mask_pred_results = outputs["pred_masks"]     # (B, Q, H/4, W/4)
mask_pred_results = F.interpolate(
    mask_pred_results, size=(images.tensor.shape[-2], images.tensor.shape[-1]),
    mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)     # → (B, Q, H_pad, W_pad)

del outputs

for mask_cls_result, mask_pred_result, input_per_image, image_size in zip(
        mask_cls_results, mask_pred_results, batched_inputs, images.image_sizes):
    height = input_per_image.get("height", image_size[0])
    width = input_per_image.get("width", image_size[1])
```

[mask2former_model.py:239-260](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L239-L260)

```python
if self.sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference:
    mask_pred_result = retry_if_cuda_oom(sem_seg_postprocess)(
        mask_pred_result, image_size, height, width)
    mask_cls_result = mask_cls_result.to(mask_pred_result)

if self.semantic_on:
    r = retry_if_cuda_oom(self.semantic_inference)(mask_cls_result, mask_pred_result)
    if not self.sem_seg_postprocess_before_inference:
        r = retry_if_cuda_oom(sem_seg_postprocess)(r, image_size, height, width)
    processed_results[-1]["sem_seg"] = r

if self.panoptic_on:
    panoptic_r = retry_if_cuda_oom(self.panoptic_inference)(mask_cls_result, mask_pred_result)
    processed_results[-1]["panoptic_seg"] = panoptic_r

if self.instance_on:
    instance_r = retry_if_cuda_oom(self.instance_inference)(mask_cls_result, mask_pred_result)
    processed_results[-1]["instances"] = instance_r
```

关键行为：

- `F.interpolate` 一次性把整个 batch 的 Q 张 mask 从 1/4 分辨率拉到 padding 尺寸；`del outputs` 主动释放 `aux_outputs` 等已无用的中间张量，为后面的高清后处理腾显存。
- `sem_seg_postprocess(x, img_size, output_h, output_w)`（detectron2 提供）负责「padding 画布 → 网络输入尺寸 → 原图尺寸」的裁剪+插值；`height/width` 缺省时退回 `image_size`。
- `pred_logits` 末维是 \(K+1=134\)（含 no-object），各推理分支自行决定怎么处理最后一维。
- 三个 `if` 互相独立：COCO 配置三个开关全开（[maskformer2_R50_bs16_50ep.yaml:40-43](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/configs/coco/panoptic-segmentation/maskformer2_R50_bs16_50ep.yaml#L40-L43)），所以 demo 输出同时含三个键——呼应 u1-l4 的观察。
- 每个分支都包了 `retry_if_cuda_oom`：高分辨率下任何一步 OOM 都有三段降级（直接算 → 清缓存重试 → 搬 CPU），细节在 u10-l2。

三个 `*_inference` 方法的内部逻辑（einsum 融合、topk 重打分、段合并）分别由 u6-l1/l2/l3 精讲，本讲不展开。

**答案**：`image_size`（来自 `images.image_sizes`）是「网络输入尺寸」，即模型实际看到的缩放后尺寸；`batched_inputs` 里的 `height/width` 是 mapper 透传的「原图尺寸」，推理输出应对齐的最终目标。`get` 的缺省值处理的是输入 dict 没带原图尺寸的边缘情况。

### 4.3 prepare_targets：把 Instances 变成 labels + masks

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

criterion 的输入不是 detectron2 的 `Instances`，而是朴素的 `list[dict]`，每图一个 dict，只含两个键：`"labels"`（该图 N 个 GT 的连续类别 id，形状 `(N,)`）和 `"masks"`（二值 mask 张量，形状 `(N, H_pad, W_pad)`）。`prepare_targets` 就是这最后一跳的「格式转换器」。

最关键的设计决策：GT mask 的尺寸适配用的是 **左上角对齐 zero-pad**，而不是 resize。原因：u2-l3 讲过 mapper 输出的 `gt_masks` 已经是网络输入尺寸（LSJ 下 1024×1024）的 tensor，与图像经受的几何变换完全一致；到 padding 尺寸只差右侧/下侧补零，与 `ImageList` 对图像的处理方式完全对称——**图像怎么 pad，GT 就怎么 pad**。如果用插值 resize，GT mask 的二值边界会被破坏，且与图像网格错位。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
prepare_targets(targets=list[Instances], images=ImageList)
  h_pad, w_pad = images.tensor.shape[-2:]        # padding 尺寸
  for 每张图的 Instances:
      gt_masks = instances.gt_masks               # (N, H, W) tensor
      padded = zeros(N, h_pad, w_pad)             # 全 0 画布
      padded[:, :H, :W] = gt_masks                # 左上角原样贴入
      new_targets.append({
          "labels": instances.gt_classes,         # (N,)
          "masks":  padded,                       # (N, H_pad, W_pad)
      })
  return new_targets
```

注意 batch 内每张图的 N 可以不同（图片里对象数不同），`labels`/`masks` 是按图成对的列表，匹配与损失都按图处理后汇总（criterion 里 `num_masks = sum(len(t["labels"]) for t in targets)`，见 [criterion.py:225](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/criterion.py#L225)）。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

[mask2former/maskformer_model.py:264-278](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/maskformer_model.py#L264-L278)

```python
def prepare_targets(self, targets, images):
    h_pad, w_pad = images.tensor.shape[-2:]          # ① padding 尺寸
    new_targets = []
    for targets_per_image in targets:
        # pad gt
        gt_masks = targets_per_image.gt_masks        # ② (N, H, W) tensor（来自 mapper）
        padded_masks = torch.zeros(
            (gt_masks.shape[0], h_pad, w_pad),
            dtype=gt_masks.dtype, device=gt_masks.device)   # ③ 新画布，类型/设备对齐
        padded_masks[:, : gt_masks.shape[1], : gt_masks.shape[2]] = gt_masks  # ④ 左上角贴入
        new_targets.append(
            {
                "labels": targets_per_image.gt_classes,     # ⑤ 连续类别 id
                "masks": padded_masks,
            }
        )
    return new_targets
```

- ① 尺寸取自 `images.tensor` 而不是原图——GT mask 必须与 `pred_masks` 上采样后共享同一画布，损失才能逐像素对齐。
- ② `gt_masks` 是**tensor**。LSJ mapper 里 `instances.gt_masks = masks.tensor`（`BitMasks` 的裸 tensor，见 [coco_panoptic_new_baseline_dataset_mapper.py:157-160](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/data/dataset_mappers/coco_panoptic_new_baseline_dataset_mapper.py#L157-L160)）；如果喂进来的是 `PolygonMasks`（多边形列表，无 `.shape[1]`/`.shape[2]`），第 ④ 行会直接 `AttributeError`/索引错误——这是自己写 mapper 时最常见的坑。
- ③ `torch.zeros` 保证 pad 区是 0（非对象），`dtype`/`device` 与 GT 一致。
- ④ 切片赋值：`[:, :H, :W]` 把整张 GT mask 不做任何缩放地放到画布左上角，右侧/下侧留 0。
- ⑤ `gt_classes` 是 mapper 阶段已映射好的**连续 id**（0..132），与 `pred_logits` 的前 K 维直接对应；全景标注原始的 `category_id` 到连续 id 的映射发生在数据注册/mapper 侧（u2-l2、u2-l3），到这里已经是干净的张量。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：如果某图的 GT mask 尺寸大于 padding 尺寸（例如手工喂数据时忘了先做 LSJ resize），会发生什么？

**答案**：第 ④ 行切片赋值中 `gt_masks.shape[1] > h_pad` 时，`padded_masks[:, :H, :W]` 的目标区域比源小，PyTorch 会因形状不匹配抛 `RuntimeError`。这天然起到了「GT 必须与图像同尺寸」的断言作用。

**练习 2**：为什么 pad 出来的全 0 背景对损失是「正确的」监督信号，而不是「噪声」？

**答案**：`ImageList` 对图像 pad 的区域同样是 0，模型在这些像素上的预测没有任何图像依据；GT mask 在此处为 0 表示「不属于任何对象」，恰好与「预测的所有 mask 在此处都应接近 0」对应。更重要的是，匈牙利匹配在 mask 代价里会避开纯背景差异的歧义（u5-l1 详解）。反过来说，batch 内不同图的 padding 量不同，若用全图逐像素损失而不加处理，短图会被更多 pad 区稀释——这就是 criterion 里按「mask 数量」而非「像素数」归一化的动机之一（u5-l2 详解）。

**练习 3**：`prepare_targets` 为什么需要 `images` 参数？只用 `batched_inputs` 里的信息不够吗？

**答案**：`batched_inputs[i]["image"]` 的形状是 padding **前**的网络输入尺寸，而 GT mask 必须落在 padding **后**的画布上（与 `images.tensor`、上采样后的 `pred_masks` 对齐）。`H_pad/W_pad` 只有 `ImageList` 知道，所以必须把 `images` 传进来。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `build_model(cfg)` → `from_config(cfg)` → `__init__(**dict)`：`from_config` 构建 backbone、sem_seg_head、`HungarianMatcher` 与 `SetCriterion`，并把三个损失权重同时用作匹配代价与损失加权；深监督把 `weight_dict` 从 3 个键展开成 30 个。
- `forward` = 公共前奏（归一化 → `ImageList` padding → backbone → sem_seg_head）+ 按 `self.training` 二分流：训练返回加权过滤后的 loss dict，推理返回逐图 `list[dict]`。
- 训练分支把 mapper 产出的 `Instances`（`gt_classes` + tensor 型 `gt_masks`）经 `prepare_targets` 转成 `{"labels", "masks"}`；GT mask 用**左上角 zero-pad** 对齐到 padding 画布，与图像的处理方式严格对称，绝不 resize。
- 推理分支先把 `pred_masks` 双线性上采样到 padding 尺寸并 `del outputs` 省显存，再按 `SEMANTIC_ON / PANOPTIC_ON / INSTANCE_ON` 三个独立开关把结果分发给三个 `*_inference`（细节在单元六）。
- 三种尺寸贯穿始终：原图（`height/width`）、网络输入（`image_sizes`）、padding（`images.tensor`），后处理就是在这三者之间换算。

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.
